steps.loadFixture: open a fresh page, then the hand-written fixture `fixture` (tab900 or bp768, files under scripts/ui-editor-gate/reference/) through Paste: the markup field, Open pasted code. steps.view: as before: click the view button Desktop, Tablet or Phone (the selection is kept).

steps.drag: as before: a real mouse drag of dx, dy window px from the centre of sel, or from the handle named by `handle` (the gate's host is 1920 x 1080, where every view is at scale 1, so a window px is a CSS px).

asserts.computed: P1 (via preview) or P2 (via export). For each width w of `at` the computed value of `prop` of `sel` equals the expected string; lengths in px are equal within `tol` px, every other value exactly. `not` lists values that must NOT be the computed value at a width. via preview: the preview's frame is set to that width and read (the page under test); via export: the files of the current export are loaded fresh in plain Chromium at that width (independent of the page). `collateral` marks a check that another element is unchanged.
asserts.noLinkUi: P5. In the editor (the element [data-editor], the code view left out): no checkbox but Include comments, no [data-dot], no element whose text, accessible name or tooltip has the word Link, Unlinked or Review (whole words, case-insensitive), no button whose name starts with Review.
asserts.barNames: P5. The visible buttons of the group Editor controls, in document order, have exactly the accessible names `names` (a count after a name, as in Review unlinked (0), is part of the name).
asserts.editList: P5. The edit list the page holds (the attribute data-edit-list of [data-editor]) has exactly the edits of `expect` in order; for each, `op` is equal; `environment` is equal ('absent': the edit has no environment field); `link` is 'absent' (no link field), 'notFalse' (absent or true) or false.
asserts.equalsList: P2. Every exported file equals, byte for byte, what the vendored engine gives (in the runner's own page) for the page's edit list replayed on the original files.
asserts.movedAt: P1. At each width of `moved` the transform of sel in the preview is a translation of about (dx, dy) CSS px (within tol; the drag's window px divided by the scale); at each width of `same` it is none.
asserts.tabSequence: P5. `area` ribbon: with the focus put just before the ribbon, Tab visits (as often as there are names plus 5) the controls of the ribbon and stops where the focus leaves it; the accessible names, in order, are exactly `names`. `area` bar: the same from the first button of the group Editor controls to where the focus leaves it.
asserts.tabOrder: as before (round 4): Tab visits every enabled ribbon control in visual order, each with a focus indicator.
asserts.pageText: P5. The text of the page (scope 'page': the body's text content and every title and aria-label; scope 'editor': the same inside [data-editor]) contains every string of `has` and none of `lacks` (case-sensitive).
asserts.ribbonNoteHidden: P5. The ribbon's note [data-ribbon-note] is hidden or empty.
asserts.textAbsent: as before: the editor's own text does not contain `contains`.
asserts.message: as before: the last status message contains `contains` (lower-cased).

asserts.ribbonEnabled: as before: every named ribbon control is enabled.

asserts.handles: as before: n resize handles are shown.

specs.name: Desktop font size: a Desktop edit of #headline (44 to 52) reaches Phone and Tablet in proportion; the computed value at 1280, 1025, 1024, 768, B+1 (641), B (640) and 390 in the preview and in the export loaded fresh equals the hand-derived truth; nothing else changes; the field shows the view's own value
Desktop font size on a page with its own tablet band (tab900: B 640, T 900): 40 to 50 gives 50 above 900, 42.5 for 641 to 900 and 35 at 640 and below, at 1280, 1024, 901, 900, 768, 641, 640 and 390
Desktop padding (tab900 #panel, 24 to 36): 36 above 640, the page's own 16 becomes 24 at 640 and below; Tablet follows Desktop
Desktop width (tab900 #panel, 480 to 600): 600 above 640 but never wider than its parent (593 at 641), the page's own 100% stays 100% (608 at 640, 358 at 390)
A Desktop colour and a Desktop font family apply at every width as written (landing #headline: #b00020 and Arial)

A Phone custom edit changes only the phone range: a font size typed in Phone (36) is 36 at 640 and 390 only; Desktop and Tablet keep 44, the Desktop view shows 44 and the Tablet view 44; the edit list carries environment phone and nothing else

A Tablet custom edit changes only the tablet range: a font size typed in Tablet (46) is 46 from 641 to 1024 only (T is 1024: the page has no tablet rule); Desktop 44 at 1025 and above, Phone 30; the edit list carries environment tablet and nothing else
A Tablet custom padding on a page with a tablet band (tab900 #panel, 24 to 30): 30 from 641 to 900, 24 above 900, the page's own 16 at 640 and below
A Tablet custom font size (46), then a Desktop one (50) on the same element: the tablet range keeps 46, Desktop gets 50 and the phone range 35 (tab900 #title)
The reverse order: a Desktop font size (50), then a Tablet custom one (46) on the same element, gives the same values (tab900 #title)
A Phone custom font size (36), then a Desktop one (52) on the same element: the Desktop edit reaches 641 and above (Tablet too) and not the phone range, which keeps 36; no refusal
A Desktop colour after a Phone custom colour is not refused and the Phone view keeps its colour: #ffcc00 in Phone, then #00aa55 in Desktop gives #00aa55 above 640 and #ffcc00 at 640 and below
